newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ciampi does not exclude mini budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi does not exclude mini budget.

text.p: Italy's Treasury and Budget Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said in an interview published on Tuesday that he did could not exclude the possibility of an additional mini-budget next year.
"I can't exclude or confirm a mini-budget. We have to see carefully what the situation is in the first few months of the new year," he told the Rome newspaper La Repubblica in an interview.
Italy's industrialists' group Confindustria on Monday told a delegation from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) that it believed Italy would need a mini-budget next year, it said in a statement.

Confindustria said measures contained in the government's 1997 budget "were not sufficient to reach the objective of a three percent ratio between the deficit and GDP and therefore an additional budget will be necessary in the coming months".
Italy needs to reach the objective to qualify for membership of Europe's planned single currency from its 1999 start.

Confindustria said the budget, which parliament must approve by the end of the month, was too heavily weighted in favour of revenue-raising and was devoid of significant measures aimed at limiting structural spending.
